Submit - I simply added a commentary on col. 3.1 to make it clear to scholars working on that papyrus that the line numbering of col. 3 now in papyri.info is based on a new reading of ll. 1 and 2 (entered via PN) and that the edition and all scholarly references to col. 3 use different line numbers. (I haven't found any help entry that would seem to fit to put that kind of information in the apparatus.)

Submit - Correction from photo: The first two lines of col. 3 are actually one single line and the text is continuous without a vacat on the papyrus. I reunited both lines and adapted the line numbering for the entire column. The error is present in the edition: The editor correctly indented Ἑρμο(ῦ) πόλει δη̣[μόσ(ιον) ϑη]σ̣(αυρὸν) to indicate that l. 1 continues, as he does elsewhere (e.g., in col. 2.15). He then, however, counted Μαξιμιανοῦ κτλ. as l. 5 instead of l. 4, also in the commentary, and the error persists in all subsequent quotations of that papyrus I looked at. Peculiarly, the only exception I came across is the entry of BL 1.211 for P.Lips. 1.84, which is correct for “l. 2” even though the source (Wilcken in APF 4, p. 482) counted with the wrong (+1) numbers, while the following lines in the same BL entry are all quoted with wrong (+1) numbers.
Unrelated to that, the LeidenPlus texts of coll. 1–3 end as if the papyrus was broken at these points. On the photo one can, however, clearly see under these columns the lines that the edition describes as follows: “Darunter ein Rest einer anderweitigen, vermutlich später auf den freien Raum geschriebenen Rechnung, enthaltend Personennamen und Summenangaben nach Litern,” implying these entries do not belong to the receipts above. I suggest using “vestig” unter columns 1–3 until the full text of these is being given, and therefore changed all three “lost.?lin” to “vestig,” deleting the “18. vac.?” under col. 1 in the process because the spaces between the individual receipts are also not marked (ed. ends with l. 17).

item.p: The ed. pr. counted Ἑρμοῦ πόλει δημόσιον θησαυρὸν as l. 2, δεκαπρώτοις κτλ. as l. 3, and so on, and subsequent scholarly references to that papyrus continued this "+1 numbering." The online image reveals that Ἑρμοῦ πόλει δημόσιον θησαυρὸν still belongs to l. 1. (M. Stern)
